column1: # premise-dairy: Plain, whole, cultured; milk and cultures are the only ingredients.

column4: Whole fat on the front; 'ultra-pasteurized' printed near the date means skip.
column5: Ultra-pasteurized means heated at or above 280 °F for at least 2 seconds, and WAPF lists ultrapasteurized milk products to avoid.

column4: Ingredient list reads milk and named cultures, with no sugar, pectin or flavors.
column5: Cornucopia scores yogurts down for flavors, preservatives and pectin or gums, and plain tubs let the shopper control sugar.

column4: Skip when 'organic sugar' or 'natural flavors' sits in the ingredient list.
column5: Cornucopia gives zero points to yogurts listing only organic sugar, and organic rules permit natural flavors.

column4: Ingredients: milk and kefir cultures only; unsweetened word on the front.
column5: WAPF names whole yogurt and kefir among the cultured dairy it recommends.

column4: Ingredients: cream and cultures; no starch, gums or flavor words.
column5: WAPF puts cream, cultured cream and sour cream with additives on its avoid list.

column4: Cream is the only ingredient; 'ultra-pasteurized' not stamped on the carton.
column5: Ultra-pasteurized cream is on WAPF avoid list; ultra-pasteurized means 280 °F for 2 seconds.

column4: Oil or sugar listed ahead of any dairy word in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF lists non-dairy creamers and imitation whipped cream made with vegetable oils under avoid.

column4: Ingredients: cream, salt; skip any 'natural flavor' entry.
column5: WAPF rates pasteurized butter without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.

column4: Ingredient reads butterfat or clarified butter alone; no oil blended in.
column5: WAPF counts ghee without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, among its good butters.

column4: Name reads 'cheese', never 'cheese food' or 'cheese product'.
column5: Pasteurized process cheese is cheeses ground and mixed with heat, a different standard of identity than the cheese itself.

column4: 'Pasteurized process cheese food' or 'cheese product' printed on the wrapper.
column5: Process cheese is comminuted and mixed with heat from one or more cheeses, not a single made cheese.

column4: Ingredients: cream, milk, salt, cultures; gums such as carob or guar missing.
column5: Cornucopia counts pectins and gums as thickener additives that lower a dairy score.

column4: Cultures named; carrageenan or gums not in the ingredient list.
column5: Cornucopia graded dairy on thickeners and carrageenan, which it calls a potential inflammatory agent.

column4: Cream, milk, eggs, sugar named; vanilla bean or extract, no 'flavor' words.
column5: WAPF advises avoiding ice cream made with extenders, powdered milk, agave or natural flavors.

column4: Goat or sheep named on the front; ingredients are milk and cultures.
Oil (sunflower, canola) or gellan listed after the oats and water.
column5: WAPF says to avoid imitation milk products.

column4: Almonds and water only; carrageenan, gums or 'natural flavors' listed means skip.
column5: Organic rules permit natural flavors, which cover products of heating or enzymolysis.

column4: 'Soy protein isolate' in the ingredients; organic soybeans and water only passes.
column5: WAPF says industrially processed soy protein and isolates carry natural toxins and ones created by processing.

column4: Aseptic carton printed on the pack; coconut and water alone passes.
column5: WAPF lists coconut products in aseptic boxes under avoid.

column4: Can with coconut and water only; BPA-free lining stated.
column5: WAPF recommends canned whole coconut milk without additives, preferably in BPA-free containers; BPA-free claims are not standardized.

column4: 'Vegetable oil' leads the ingredient list of any tub or stick.
column5: WAPF lists all margarines, spreads and partially hydrogenated shortenings under avoid.

column4: Palm, canola or 'vegetable oil blend' in the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers most commercial vegetable and seed oils and spreads.

column4: 'Hydrogenated' or vegetable oil on a canned or tub topping.
column5: WAPF lists canned whipped cream and imitation whipped cream made with vegetable oils under avoid.

column1: # premise-oils: One named oil, dated and dark-bottled; unnamed vegetable oil blends are the skip.

column4: One oil named on the label: olive, coconut or avocado, not a blend.
column5: WAPF avoids most commercial vegetable and seed oils, so a single named oil is the alternative.

column4: Bottle reads 'vegetable oil' or lists soybean, canola, corn, cottonseed.
column5: WAPF avoid list names cottonseed, soy, corn and canola oils.

column4: Harvest date printed, dark glass or tin, 'extra virgin' on the front.
column5: UC Davis says dark glass and tins protect oil and a harvest date shows freshness.

column4: Harvest or production date printed; virgin, not 'refined', on the label.
column5: UC Davis advises choosing avocado oil close to its harvest or production date.

column4: 'Cold pressed' or 'expeller pressed' printed on the front of the bottle.
column5: Organic handling bars volatile synthetic solvents such as those used in oil extraction.

column4: Rendered fat is the only ingredient; hydrogenated not listed.
Smell of stale nuts or Play-Doh on opening; clear plastic bottle gets skipped.
column5: UC Davis names stale nuts or Play-Doh as the smell of rancid oil and clear plastic as least protective.

column1: # premise-grains-bread: One whole grain named first; sourdough over enriched; organic for glyphosate.

column4: Ingredient list is one grain, with 'whole' before its name.
column5: WAPF says grains are sprayed with glyphosate just before harvest, so buy organic.

column4: Ingredient reads whole grain oats; instant packets listing flavor or sugar fail.
column5: Organic bars excluded methods, and WAPF says grains are soaked, sprouted or fermented to neutralize phytic acid.

column4: Ingredient list reads rice alone; rice syrup and rice cereal are separate skips.
column5: Consumer Reports found arsenic in organic and conventional rice products alike; organic still rules out excluded methods.

column4: Grain named on the front, with no seasoning packet in the box.
'Wild rice' is the sole ingredient; no blend with white rice.
USDA Organic seal on the cornmeal; 'degerminated' on the bag means skip.
column5: Corn is on the Non-GMO Project High-Risk List, and organic bars excluded methods.

column4: One legume named; soak-and-cook directions printed on the bag.
column5: WAPF says legumes are soaked or sprouted to neutralize phytic acid and enzyme inhibitors.

column4: Dry bag lists beans alone; canned label states a BPA-free lining.
column5: BPA-free can claims are not standardized, so a dry bag removes the question.

column4: Durum or whole wheat semolina named; no 'enriched' entry in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF advises avoiding white flour products, and says grains are dried with glyphosate.

column4: 'Stone ground' or 'whole' on the bag; 'bleached' or 'enriched' means skip.
column5: WAPF says avoid white flour and white flour products.

column4: Almond, einkorn or coconut named alone; no starch listed.
'100% whole' beside a named grain; 'multigrain' alone is not enough.
Extruded o's, flakes or puffs, or 'natural' printed on the box.
column5: WAPF says extrusion distorts grain proteins, and Cornucopia flags misuse of the term natural on cereal.

column4: Starter named in ingredients; baker's yeast, vinegar or 'sourdough flavor' means skip.
column5: WAPF says genuine sourdough fermentation breaks down gluten.

column4: 'Sprouted' before each grain in the ingredient list, not flour first.
column5: WAPF says seeds and grains are soaked, sprouted, fermented or leavened to neutralize phytic acid.

column4: 'Enriched wheat flour', sugar or soybean oil near the top of the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF says avoid white flour and white flour products.

column4: Starches and gums stacked in the ingredient list; one flour first passes.
'Dough conditioners' or 'enriched' in ingredients; sprouted or sourdough on the bag.
column5: WAPF says avoid white flour products and quick-rise breads.

column1: # premise-sweeteners: Name the sweetener on the label; unnamed sugar and syrups are the skip.

column4: 'Dehydrated cane juice' or organic cane sugar named, not 'sugar' alone.
column5: WAPF lists dehydrated sugar cane juice among best sweeteners and white sugar under avoid.

column4: 'Pure maple syrup' only; corn syrup in the ingredients means imitation.
column5: WAPF lists maple syrup as a best sweetener and imitation syrups under avoid.

column4: 'Raw' and 'unfiltered' on the jar; cloudy with pollen, not clear.
column5: Ultra-filtration removes all pollen, and pollen is the only sure way to trace honey to a place.

column4: Ingredient reads molasses or dehydrated cane juice, no 'sugar' ahead of it.
column5: WAPF names molasses and dehydrated sugar cane juice among its best sweeteners.

column4: Plant named in ingredients: date, coconut or sorghum, not 'natural sweetener'.
column5: WAPF lists coconut sugar, date sugar and sorghum syrup among best sweeteners.

column4: Corn syrup, agave or brown rice syrup anywhere in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF avoid list names corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup, brown rice syrup and agave.

column1: # premise-nuts-seeds: Raw or dry-roasted, sealed, ingredient list is the nut or seed alone.

column4: Sealed package, ingredient list the nut alone; skip open bins.
column5: WAPF rates fresh organic raw nuts in sealed packages, not from bins, as best.

column4: 'Raw' or 'dry roasted' printed; 'oil roasted' or coated means skip.
column5: WAPF counts raw and dry-roasted nuts as good and nut mixtures with sugar or flavorings as avoid.

column4: Ingredients: nuts, maybe salt; sugar, palm or 'hydrogenated' words mean skip.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers nut butters with hydrogenated oils, sugar, agave or flavorings.

column4: Raw seeds sealed with a date; the seed is the lone ingredient.
column5: WAPF rates fresh organic raw seeds in sealed packages as best.

column4: Sugar, yogurt chips or vegetable oil listed beside the nuts.
column5: WAPF avoid list names nut mixtures with partially hydrogenated oils, sugar or flavorings.

column4: Unfortified flakes list yeast only; 'fortified' means added synthetic vitamins.
column5: WAPF advises avoiding synthetic vitamins and foods containing them.

column1: # premise-canned-jarred: Glass or stated BPA-free cans; ingredients are the food, salt, named oil.

column4: Label states BPA-free lining; ingredients are the food, water, salt.
column5: BPA-free can claims have no national standard, so a stated claim is a floor, not proof.

column4: Tomatoes first, oil named, no sugar or 'natural flavors' in the list.
column5: WAPF rates sauces with natural ingredients and no MSG as good and most commercial sauces as avoid.

column4: Glass jar; vegetables, oil by name, salt and spices, nothing else.
column5: WAPF lists most commercial sauces under avoid and natural-ingredient sauces without MSG as good.

column4: One sea vegetable named; no oil or 'natural flavor' in the ingredients.
Chickpeas, tahini, olive oil named; canola or soybean oil means skip.
column5: WAPF avoid list names canola and soy oils.

column1: # premise-snacks-condiments: Short list you could stock yourself; no natural flavors, no unnamed oil.

column4: One herb named on the jar; no blend listing citric acid or MSG.
column5: WAPF avoid list covers spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid or hydrolyzed protein.

column4: Whole seeds or sticks of one spice named; no 'spices' blend.
column5: WAPF rates non-irradiated spices and blends without additives as best.

column4: Grey, pink or beige colour; iodized or free-flowing listed means skip.
column5: WAPF lists unrefined salt in light grey, pink, red or beige as best and iodized salt as avoid.

column4: 'Aluminum-free' on the tin; ingredients: cornstarch, baking soda, cream of tartar.
column5: WAPF advises avoiding aluminum-containing baking powder.

column4: 'Raw' and 'unfiltered' printed; cloudy strands of mother at the bottom.
column5: WAPF lists organic raw vinegars as best.

column4: 'Distilled white vinegar' printed; apple cider, wine or balsamic named passes.
column5: WAPF avoid list names distilled vinegar.

column4: Tomatoes, vinegar, spices listed; no 'natural flavors' entry.
column5: WAPF rates organic mustard and ketchup sweetened with organic sugar or natural sweeteners as good.

column4: 'Naturally brewed' on the label; hydrolyzed protein or caramel color listed means skip.
column5: WAPF lists naturally fermented soy sauce as good and liquid amino acids as avoid.

column4: Soybean or canola oil named as the first oil on the label.
column5: WAPF avoid list names soy and canola oils.

column4: 'Hydrogenated' or 'enriched' wheat flour in ingredients; seeds and named oil pass.
column5: WAPF avoid list includes commercially processed crackers.

column4: 'Enriched flour' first on the label, with a corn syrup or vegetable oil line.
column5: WAPF avoid list includes white flour products.

column4: Brown rice syrup, protein isolate or 'natural flavors' in the ingredient list.
column5: WAPF avoid list names brown rice syrup, and natural flavor covers heated or enzyme products.

column4: Potatoes or corn, olive or coconut oil named, salt; nothing else.
column5: WAPF avoid list names most commercial vegetable and seed oils.

column4: Puffed grain with flavor coating, 'natural flavor' or syrup in ingredients.
column5: WAPF says extrusion distorts grain proteins.

column1: # premise-beverages: Water, tea, coffee beans; sugar or natural flavors listed means skip.

column4: 'Spring water' printed with the named spring location, not 'purified'.
column5: A spring water label must be collected at the spring or a bore hole tapping it, with the spring location identified.

column4: Whole beans, roast date stamped, USDA Organic seal.
Leaves or herbs named alone; 'natural flavors' not in the ingredients.
column5: Natural flavor includes products of roasting, heating or enzymolysis, so a flavored blend is not just leaves.

column4: 'From concentrate' or 'juice cocktail' on the front, sugar listed.
column5: WAPF avoid list names fruit juices and concentrated juices.

column4: Sugar, caramel color or 'natural flavors' in the ingredients.
column5: WAPF avoid list names soft drinks.

column4: Refrigerated glass bottle with 'raw' printed on the label.
column5: WAPF recommends organic lacto-fermented beverages in glass jars.

column4: Coconut water the sole ingredient; canned, not aseptic box.
column5: WAPF lists canned coconut water as good and coconut products in aseptic boxes as avoid.
